figures.caption:
A six-cell example of prescribed
metric work. Each direct cell-energy derivative agrees with incoming
flux minus outgoing flux plus the coefficient work term. The curves
illustrate the exact finite identity for a prescribed background.

The centered derivative has a Nyquist
zero, while a fixed resolved mode approaches its continuum frequency
with second-order error. The left panel is the one-dimensional symbol;
the right panel tests a fixed mode under refinement.
The regular triad sector and a separate finite particle gauge patch. Invertibility is a hypothesis of each reduction, and a singular boundary changes the rank of its constraint matrix.

A three-dimensional sphere and its tangent directions, together with the finite Dirac projection. The projection annihilates the specified constraint gradients while retaining physical tangent directions.
A fresh finite particle experiment contrasts resolved implicit steps with an incomplete-solve control. Its numerical residuals test the preservation mechanism within the specified model and range.

The horizon equation and the domain of the charged Painlev\'e--Gullstrand chart are different conditions. The benchmark crosses the outer horizon while remaining above the turning surface. The extremal and superextremal curves illustrate the change in the number and multiplicity of horizon roots.

The mass density and mass flux resolve into the two scalar characteristic channels. The outgoing characteristic and its contribution to the coordinate mass density degenerate at $v=1$. These are exact algebraic profiles, not a newly evolved collapse solution.

Archived event coordinates under radial refinement, together with the exact expansion and characteristic sign change at $v=1$. The event table is replotted from retained data. No new scalar-collapse evolution was performed for this figure.
